record.paper_title: Some problems and conjectures about L2-invariants
record.original_question: For a group G, a normal chain {G_i} with trivial intersection, and a matrix A ∈ M_{r,s}(QG), does the Fuglede-Kadison determinant over G always equal the limit of the Fuglede-Kadison determinants over the quotients G/G_i, namely det_{N(G)}(r_A^{(2)}) = lim_i det_{N(G/G_i)}(r_{A[i]}^{(2)})?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.3 (Approximation Conjecture for Fuglede-Kadison determinants). A group G satisfies the Approximation Conjecture for Fuglede-Kadison determinants if for any normal chain {Gi} and any matrix A ∈ Mr,s(QG) we get for the Fuglede-Kadison determinant detN(G)(r(2)A) = lim i∈I detN(G/Gi)(r(2)A[i]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a discrete group and let $\mathcal{N}(G)$ denote its group von Neumann algebra, equipped with the canonical trace $\mathrm{tr}_{\mathcal{N}(G)}$. For a matrix $A \in M_{r,s}(\mathbb{Q}G)$, let $r_A^{(2)} \colon \ell^2(G)^r \to \ell^2(G)^s$ be the bounded operator given by right multiplication with $A$, and let $\det_{\mathcal{N}(G)}(r_A^{(2)})$ denote its Fuglede–Kadison determinant.

Suppose $\{G_i\}_{i \in I}$ is a normal chain in $G$, i.e. a descending sequence of normal subgroups of finite index (or, more generally, a cofinal directed system of normal subgroups) with trivial intersection $\bigcap_{i} G_i = \{1\}$. For each $i$, let $A[i] \in M_{r,s}(\mathbb{Q}[G/G_i])$ be the image of $A$ under the projection $\mathbb{Q}G \to \mathbb{Q}[G/G_i]$, and let $r_{A[i]}^{(2)}$ be the corresponding operator on $\ell^2(G/G_i)^{r,s}$ with Fuglede–Kadison determinant $\det_{\mathcal{N}(G/G_i)}(r_{A[i]}^{(2)})$ taken in the group von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{N}(G/G_i)$.

Question: Does the equality
$$\det\nolimits_{\mathcal{N}(G)}\!\bigl(r_A^{(2)}\bigr) \;=\; \lim_{i \in I}\, \det\nolimits_{\mathcal{N}(G/G_i)}\!\bigl(r_{A[i]}^{(2)}\bigr)$$
hold for every group $G$, every such normal chain $\{G_i\}$, and every matrix $A \in M_{r,s}(\mathbb{Q}G)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The approximation problem for Fuglede–Kadison determinants over normal chains is a long-standing open conjecture in the theory of L²-invariants. Approximation of L²-Betti numbers (Lück's theorem) is known for residually finite groups, and convergence of determinants has been established in special cases (e.g. amenable groups, sofic groups under positivity hypotheses, and under uniform integrability conditions), but the general statement for arbitrary groups and arbitrary normal chains with trivial intersection is not known to be proved. No search result indicates a full resolution.

status_evidence.title: Fuglede–Kadison Determinants and Sofic Entropy
status_evidence.snippet: Approximation results for Fuglede–Kadison determinants on sofic groups under positivity hypotheses.
status_evidence.claim: Partial approximation results exist for sofic groups but the general approximation conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: Lehmer's conjecture and the Fuglede-Kadison determinant – SPP 2026
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses determinant conjectures in the setting of L²-invariants.
status_evidence.claim: Determinant approximation conjectures are stated as open problems.
